summary.headline: Recurse intrigues AI builders (mostly “maybe”) but private-alpha clarity and docs depth lag LangChain/LlamaIndex in this bakeoff.
top_friction: Private alpha / waitlist uncertainty about when they can actually use it
Hard to find concrete use cases, agent.yaml / schema, and deep technical examples
Some pages feel empty until scroll; key content not above the fold
Value prop vs LangChain/LlamaIndex not immediately differentiated for specialized-agent builders
top_strengths: Clear, intriguing promise: serverless harness + specialized/composable agents
Easy first hit on homepage and paths into Examples / docs when pages load
CLI / quickstart-style cues feel actionable when visible
summary.conversion_outlook: Across 66 finished sessions (9 hung): Recurse product was 2 yes / 18 maybe / 1 no; LangChain 0 yes / 18 maybe / 3 no; LlamaIndex 1 yes / 18 maybe / 5 no. Interest is real but commitment is soft—users stay in maybe until access and docs feel production-ready.

recommendations.action: Publish a concrete public-access timeline (or guest sandbox) past private alpha/waitlist.
recommendations.rationale: The dominant soft-no is inability to try the product now.

recommendations.action: Surface 2–3 end-to-end specialized-agent examples with agent.yaml / schema above the fold.
recommendations.rationale: Builders repeatedly struggled to find concrete technical proof.

recommendations.action: Sharpen differentiation vs LangChain and LlamaIndex in one homepage sentence.
recommendations.rationale: Bakeoff users compared stacks immediately; Recurse’s unique harness story must land in seconds.

recommendations.action: Ensure Examples/docs paint meaningful content without requiring scroll or flaky loads.
recommendations.rationale: Empty-first-screen moments tank confidence for technical evaluators.

summary.segment_fit_rationale: AI Solutions Architects, Lead AI Engineers, PMs, researchers, and DevRel personas map well to Recurse’s agent-harness pitch. Fit is capped by alpha access friction and thinner proof versus mature competitor sites.
